name: AMFI - Amsterdam Fashion Institute (English programme)
overview: You start with the foundations of the fashion industry and a personal and professional development line, then work towards one of three specialisations: Fashion & Design, Fashion & Branding or Fashion & Management. Teaching is built on practical assignments and projects, with at least 16 contact hours a week in year one, coaching throughout, and collaboration between students from different specialisations. Sustainability, diversity and digitalisation run through the curriculum. Years three and four add an internship and minor electives, and the programme works with companies from the fashion industry.

name: European School of Physiotherapy
overview: Year one builds on the human body, movement, communication and clinical reasoning, and year two moves to more complex patient cases. Theory and practical classes run in small groups with close guidance from lecturers, and you practise assessing and treating patients. Clinical internships start with a summer placement in year one and continue with two in year two, in different healthcare settings and cultural contexts. Year three includes specialised courses, a minor, research projects and professional assignments. Graduates work as physiotherapists in international healthcare or continue to a master's.

name: Sport Studies (track ISMB)
overview: You study sport management, marketing, finance and sport psychology, together with research and advice methods, running projects and personal development. About half the classes are practical sport sessions and half are theory lectures, and year one includes two international field trips. Three internships are built in: a 10-week operational placement in year two and two 20-week strategic placements in year four, at sport organisations in the Netherlands and abroad. Year three adds a professional specialisation and a minor, and the degree ends with a thesis based on a graduation project. Graduates work in the international sport industry or continue to a master's such as Sport Business & Leadership.

name: Liberal Arts and Sciences
overview: You study the sciences, social sciences and humanities side by side, learning the facts of each field and how to link them. Seminars are capped at 25 students, and classes take on big questions such as globalisation and climate change, combining analytical skills with applied experience. You major in one of the three areas, and an optional honours programme is open to Dutch and international students. The degree is run jointly by two Amsterdam universities, VU and UvA, in a multicultural city with international companies and institutions. It prepares you for decision-making roles in business, government, policy or academia.

name: Applied Mathematics
overview: The first years build calculus, linear algebra, simulation and statistics, and you learn to program in MATLAB, Python and AIMMS to turn real-world problems into mathematical models. Much of the work is project-based, often for outside companies, and AI is used as a tool in solving them. Two internships are part of the degree, with companies in the Brainport Eindhoven region, and you study on the Eindhoven University of Technology campus. In year three you can specialise in data science. Graduates work as mathematicians in organisations of many kinds or move on to a master's.

name: Applied Physics
overview: The early years cover mathematics, optics, mechanics, thermodynamics, atomic and nuclear physics, electromagnetism, quantum mechanics, measurement technology and programming. Teaching mixes lectures with laboratory experiments in well-equipped facilities and projects such as building a working multimeter, and later assignments come from companies and research groups. You study on the Eindhoven University of Technology campus and can choose between a structured route and more freedom. Graduates work as physics researchers, product developers or process-optimisation consultants at employers such as TNO, ASML, Canon, DAF and Bosch or in hospital laboratories, and a master's is also possible.

name: Automotive Engineering
overview: You study mathematics, physics, mechanics, electronics, programming, vehicle design and simulation, and measurement and testing. Theory is tied to real vehicles: you move from small model cars in year one to building a complete low-energy vehicle by the end of year two, with lab measurements feeding back into class. Year three brings a 20-week internship and a minor, such as Motorsport Engineering, and year four takes real questions from industry in Helmond. Most graduates enter the automotive sector, with employers such as DAF and VDL, while others go into high-tech industries like semiconductors, or into a master's in System Design or a pre-master at TU/e.

name: Circus and Performance Art
overview: Training centres on studio work in the circus discipline you choose, supplemented by trampoline, acrobatics, rigging basics and stage presence. Guest artists from abroad come in for intensive teaching periods, and you work on projects with students of dance, theatre, music and visual arts, since the school shares its Tilburg campus with many other arts programmes. In the third year a minor lets you train away from the school for a while, and performances and internships give professional experience. Graduates work as independent or company performers, form their own companies, or take technical and creative roles such as rigger, light or sound technician, stage designer or choreographer.

name: Communication - International Communication Management
overview: You begin with the basics of communication theory and its use, branding and media strategy, intercultural communication, research methods, presentation skills and creative writing, and specialise in later years. Classes are interactive, and you work in teams on real projects and campaigns for clients while building collaboration, leadership and feedback skills. An internship and a semester abroad at one of Fontys' partner universities are part of the experience, in a multicultural classroom on the Eindhoven campus. Graduates become communication advisors, content managers, PR specialists, brand managers or marketing consultants, and many continue to a master's.

name: Dance - Dance Arts in Context
overview: Daily studio classes build technique across contemporary, urban and other styles, alongside theory on dance history and communication and on social topics such as inclusivity, gender, body positivity and racism. You make and perform work in collaborative projects with national and international partners and with students from other art programmes on the Zwijsenplein campus, which holds many arts courses. You follow one of three profiles: Contemporary, Contemporary Urban or Choreography. Graduates work in the performing arts and wider society, drawing on an international dance network; alumni have danced with companies such as the Martha Graham Company, taught, or combined dance with psychology and therapy.

name: Finance & Control
overview: The first year spans finance and accounting, marketing, business management, logistics, risk management, data analytics and strategic management, after which you choose your own specialisation. Learning is project-based, with assignments for real companies from the first year onward, a compulsory internship, and classes of no more than 30 students in Venlo. Year three offers internship and minor options abroad, supported by a network of partner universities and regional companies. Graduates work as controllers, financial managers, financial analysts, data analysts or business advisors, often at the company where they interned.

name: Applied Science - Chemistry and Chemical Engineering
overview: Biology, chemistry and technology are taught side by side, and during the first two years you pick three theme modules to steer towards areas such as biomedical applications, pharmaceutical development, sustainable materials or water treatment. Lab work with professional equipment happens every week, in small classes, and the final year centres on a ten-month research project. Biomedical Engineering is available as a specialisation from the end of year one, and year three leaves room for an internship, a minor or pre-master's courses. The Brainport Eindhoven setting links you to companies such as Philips Healthcare and BASF and to local hospitals. Graduates go into laboratory research, product development or diagnostics, or on to a master's.

name: Electrical and Electronic Engineering
overview: Year one covers electronics fundamentals, programming and mathematics, with you building working devices such as volume controllers, metal detectors or vending machines; year two adds signal processing and power electronics. Teaching is mostly project-based, with team prototypes, lab work and a portfolio rather than many exams. A work placement in year three and a graduation internship in year four sit around a minor, and in year four you specialise in Electronic Systems, Embedded Systems or Innovation Engineering. Graduates become designers, advisors, test engineers or embedded software engineers in fields like electric vehicles and medical devices, or go on to a master's such as Digital Technology Engineering.

name: AMSIB - International Business
overview: The first years cover Business English, economics, marketing and sales and personal and intercultural development, and in the second semester you start and run a real company as part of co-creative entrepreneurship. Lectures sit alongside real-business projects and team case competitions, and year two offers electives such as data analytics for business and crisis management. In year three you choose one of five majors, such as International Marketing and Sales or Global Business Communication, and can spend a semester on exchange at one of over 160 partner universities. Year four brings an internship at an international organisation and a thesis. Graduates move into international business roles or entrepreneurship, or on to a master's.

name: Industrial Design Engineering
overview: Design, technology and business come together, covering product design and visualisation, technical problem-solving, manufacturing and production, usability and user-centred design, and sustainability and social impact. From year one you work on live projects for real clients, in team-based studio assignments with companies, and document your results in a portfolio, with coaching from lecturers and a study coach. Year three offers an internship or minor abroad through the network of partners around the Venlo campus. Graduates work as product designers, design engineers, freelance design consultants or structural packaging designers, with employers such as Philips, Canon and Bosch, and can continue to a master in design or engineering.

name: Information Technology
overview: The first part builds a broad base in software development: programming in Java, Python, C# and JavaScript, SQL and database concepts, tools such as Git and Docker, and Agile and Scrum ways of working. Learning is project-based, applying theory to real challenges in international teams, and shaped further by internships and a graduation assignment. After about a year and a half you choose a specialisation: Business Informatics, Software Engineering, Artificial Intelligence, Cyber Security, Data Science or Embedded Software. Graduates work as software or database developers, data scientists, AI developers or security professionals, or continue their studies.

name: International Business
overview: You study four main business areas, namely marketing and sales, finance and accounting, supply chain and operations, and human resources, together with economics and general business knowledge. Lectures give the foundations and group projects apply them to realistic business situations. An international internship in another country is part of the degree, and exchange at partner universities is possible. You can study in Venlo, a smaller international community, or in Eindhoven, a technology and design hub. Graduates work as business developers, international marketers, product managers or HR managers.

name: Marketing Management - Digital Business Concepts
overview: The programme starts with marketing fundamentals, business and finance basics, consumer behaviour through business psychology, brand strategy, managing social media channels, sales processes, and e-commerce and business model development. You work on marketing projects for real companies throughout, in classes of at most 30, complete two six-month internships, and can take an exchange semester in year three before a graduation assignment. After year one you pick a focus such as digital marketing, branding, market research or international marketing, in Tilburg or Venlo. Graduates become social media managers, communication consultants, brand managers, content creators or online marketers.

name: Mechanical Engineering
overview: The early years build mechanics, thermodynamics, materials science, design and drafting, and physics applied to mechanical systems. Learning is hands-on and project-based, with extensive practical work in labs and workplaces, research assignments for companies, team projects such as a hovercraft, roller coaster or drone, and coaching for personal development. In later years you follow an Engineering, Energy or Innovation focus. The programme draws on the Brainport Eindhoven high-tech region, on a campus shared with TU/e, and on Greenport Venlo. Graduates work as engineers, sustainability project leaders, technical buyers or in medical R&D, and can continue at Fontys or TU/e.

name: Mechatronics
overview: Mechanical engineering, electrical engineering, software development and mathematics are combined, and you work with students from other engineering fields on real challenges from year one. Teaching relies on hands-on projects, modern labs, guided projects with companies and an internship. The two campuses differ: Eindhoven centres on high-tech robotics and systems in the Brainport ecosystem, while Venlo leans towards sustainability and smart manufacturing in the Greenport region. Graduates work as system architects, service engineers, industrial automation specialists, designers, control technicians, technical consultants or project managers, in sectors such as healthcare, robotics, software, R&D and maintenance, or continue to a master.

name: Medical Imaging and Radiation Therapy
overview: You study anatomy and pathology, imaging technologies such as MRI, CT, SPECT and X-ray, radiation science including protection, patient communication and care, and how to operate equipment and process scans. Year one is about orientation and teamwork, and year two moves to advanced imaging and radiation planning. Practical labs and projects sit alongside roughly 20 classroom hours a week, a 20-week internship in year three with real patients, a minor, and a graduation project with a further internship in year four. Graduates work as diagnostic radiographers, radiation therapists, imaging specialists or clinical researchers, mainly in hospitals, clinics and research settings.

name: Music - Conservatory of Music Tilburg
overview: Your main subject, taught in individual and group lessons with technique work, sits at the centre, next to ensemble playing, music theory linked to current topics, and subjects that broaden your range. There are several project weeks a year, co-creation with dance, circus and visual arts students, and performances from concert halls to public spaces. You follow either the Classical route, with a contemporary approach and room to switch creative roles, or Jazz & Creative Music, built on improvisation, your own sound and specialised ensembles; Tilburg jazz venue PARADOX offers students concerts and jam sessions. Graduates perform on stages at home and abroad, work across art forms, teach, or move into arts management and policy, or a master.

name: Physiotherapy
overview: You learn anatomy and physiology, neurology, orthopaedics and pathology, basic techniques such as movement therapy and massage, and social skills. A typical week combines 16 class hours, four project hours and 16 hours of self-study, with patient contact from year one, where you assess patients and draw up treatment plans under supervision. Internships run through the programme and finish with a final placement alongside a research project. In years three and four you choose a focus programme in Healthcare, Self-Management or Interprofessional Collaboration, plus a minor. Graduates work as physiotherapists in hospitals, nursing homes, rehabilitation centres, schools, private practices, companies, fitness centres and sports associations.

name: ICT: Information & Communication Technology
overview: The common first stage covers programming at several levels (hard coding, low code and no code), digital infrastructure and system design, data analysis and management, and current developments such as AI, data protection and the Internet of Things. You then choose from 13 specialisations, including Cyber Security, Artificial Intelligence, Game Design & Development, Robotics and User Interaction Design. Work is project-based for around 120 partner companies in the Brainport and Midpoint Brabant regions, with lab work on physical systems, a compulsory internship, a portfolio and optional study abroad. Graduates become security advisors, AI consultants, data analysts, cloud engineers, game developers or UX designers.

name: Industrial Engineering and Management
overview: You start with business economics, corporate social responsibility, production technology, process analysis and improvement, and data analysis. Learning happens through group assignments and projects at technical companies in the region, followed by a compulsory internship and a graduation project with industry partners. You choose one of five specialisations: Automotive and Mobility Management, Commercial & Organisational Excellence, Operational Excellence, Smart Industry, or Sustainability Excellence & Regenerative Design. The Brainport Eindhoven campus is shared with the Eindhoven University of Technology and has ties to companies such as ASML, Philips, VDL and DAF. Graduates work as supply chain coordinators, project managers or quality engineers.

name: Logistics Engineering
overview: The first year covers logistics and business operations, marketing and finance, warehousing and distribution, supply chain management, data analytics, IT in logistics, and simulation and automation. Learning is hands-on, with company projects from the start, company visits, lectures from industry experts and two internships; after year one you choose your own field of study. The programme is based in Venlo, a logistics hub in Europe, and year three allows an internship or minor abroad. The first year is shared with Logistics Management, International Business, Finance & Control and Marketing Management. Graduates become logistics engineers or advisors, operations or supply chain managers, or data analysts.

name: Logistics Management
overview: The first year covers marketing and business basics, finance, logistics processes, supply chain management, leadership and change management, and sustainability and ethics. You carry out company projects every semester, complete two internships, hear guest lectures from professionals and visit logistics sites, in small classes with coaching in teamwork and leadership. The first year is shared with Logistics Engineering, International Business, Finance & Control and Marketing Management, so you can switch without delay. Venlo is one of the major logistics hotspots in Europe. Graduates work as supply chain, logistics, operations or warehouse managers, sustainability advisors or distribution planners.

name: Marketing Management
overview: You begin with marketing strategy and brand management, business and finance basics, consumer behaviour and business psychology, and digital channels such as social media, plus logistics at the Venlo campus. Projects for real companies run through the whole degree, in cohorts of at most 30, along with two six-month internships at organisations worldwide and an optional exchange semester in year three. After year one you shape your own focus, for example digital marketing, branding, market research or international marketing. Graduates become content creators, digital marketing managers, brand managers or communication consultants.

name: Applied Computer Science
overview: Year one lays foundations in programming, electronics, computer architecture, networking, operating systems and mathematics, and year two adds network design and security, distributed systems, and machine learning and AI applications. Teaching is based on practical projects with fellow students on real-world problems, in teams that mirror professional settings. In year three you choose a focus and take a minor at Hanze or elsewhere, including abroad, and year four includes an internship at a national or international company. Graduates work as embedded or software engineers, IoT developers, AI engineers, cybersecurity specialists or data engineers, or continue to a master such as Smart Systems Engineering.

name: Classical Music
overview: Your main instrument or voice stays central, supported by theory classes, practical training, projects, an introduction to teaching your own instrument and entrepreneurial skills. Playing in an ensemble or orchestra is a core part of the curriculum, with masterclasses and workshops led by international musicians. Placements are arranged with partners such as the North Netherlands Orchestra and music schools, and a biennial symphony orchestra project is run with HFK Bremen. Electives follow your interests, and exchange is possible in later years. Graduates perform as ensemble musicians, orchestral players or soloists, combine performing with teaching, or continue to the Master of Music in Classical Music.

name: Creative Media & Game Technologies
overview: Year one runs in blocks on Design & Prototyping, 2D Game Development, 3D Games & Assets, and Production & Reflection; year two brings client projects using VR, AR, AI and virtual production, focus tracks, electives and a Game Lab for building a releasable game. You learn by making things in international teams rather than through exams, using the Makerspace and Spacelab for prototypes. Year three is an industry internship and year four a capstone project with external clients. Graduates work as game designers, 3D artists, UI/UX designers, game developers, technical artists or studio entrepreneurs, or continue to a master in digital transformation or international communication.

name: Design
overview: The first year introduces all six majors and builds design research, concept development, experiments with materials and media, and 2D, 3D and 4D work in studio, lab, theory and workshop classes. You then specialise in Graphic & Interaction Design, Illustration & Animation Design, Spatial Design, Time Based Design, Product Design or OffRoad, developing professional skills and learning how design shapes its context. Project weeks bring disciplines together, and minors, electives and a semester abroad or internship are possible in year three. Year four is an independent graduation project. Graduates work in independent studios, agencies or their own projects, or continue to a master or research.

name: Electrical and Electronic Engineering
overview: The first two years cover analogue and digital electronics, embedded programming, PLCs, robotics, data communication, drive systems and control systems, taught through hands-on projects for real clients, workshops at Van Doorenveste and the Hanze Makerspace. Year three includes an internship and the degree ends with a graduation project at a company or organisation. In years three and four you choose Mechatronics, Sensors & Smart Systems, or Energy & Power Electronics, and can take minors or study abroad. Graduates work as electrical, automation, embedded software, hardware or mechatronics engineers, with employers such as ASML and Philips, or continue to a master such as Smart Systems Engineering.

name: Fine Art
overview: Studio work is at the heart of the degree: in shared studios you start an artistic process and make independent work, supported by theory on contemporary art, professional practice, technical workshops and labs, and electives. Assignments come from the academy's Project Bureau and Art & Society Research Centre, there are excursions abroad, and students show work in public exhibitions and a joint graduation show. Year three offers a semester at a partner academy or an in-house minor, and honours projects are available. The academy in Groningen leads on to four master programmes. Graduates build a practice as independent artists, in their own workshop or a shared one.

name: International Business
overview: Year one introduces organisational strategy, economics, finance, marketing, business communication and intercultural competence, and year two deepens finance and accounting, operations and logistics, human resource management and international marketing, alongside a foreign language of your choice. You work on real-life projects with business clients and play business simulations such as designing a market-entry strategy. Year three is spent abroad, with a study semester at one of 120 or more partner universities and an international internship. Year four adds electives in marketing, finance or HR and consulting for an external company. Graduates become marketing, finance or account managers, consultants or entrepreneurs, or continue to an MBA.

name: International Business (3-year)
overview: The first year covers marketing, finance and accounting, supply chain management, human resource management, personal and intercultural development, business communication and an additional foreign language. You work through integrated business cases and simulation games in which you run a company. The second year takes you abroad for a semester at one of 120 or more partner universities and a placement at an organisation outside your home country. In the final year you act as a consultant for an external company, choose electives in marketing, finance or HR, and complete a graduation project on a business problem. Graduates become marketing, finance or project managers, consultants or entrepreneurs, or continue to a master or MBA.

name: International Communication
overview: You study visual communication and design, communication and media theory, crisis and reputation management, PR and marketing, public affairs, media writing and event organisation. Teaching is project-based with real clients: you design campaigns, create corporate identities and websites, and produce live talk shows, trying every production role from host to camera operator, using the Mediadesk and Medialab. Year three brings an internship abroad or an exchange semester, and you can take a minor in Language and Communication, Business and Economics, or Science and Engineering. Graduates work as PR advisors, communications coordinators, brand identity consultants, event managers or social media strategists, or continue to a master such as International Communication.

name: International Facility Management
overview: Year one introduces facility management as the creation of sustainable, innovative work environments, with service management from the customer view and human resource management. Year two focuses on service innovation and spaces in hospitality, health or sustainability, using design thinking. You work on projects with real clients, in living labs with researchers and entrepreneurs, for example on indoor climate in workspaces, and on field trips. Year three has a five-month internship as assistant manager and a minor or exchange abroad, and year four ends with a graduation project. Graduates work as facility, event, sustainability or operations managers, hospitality managers or consultants, or move on to a master.

name: International Finance & Control
overview: The early years build international finance and economics, management accounting, international business law and corporate finance. Each period pairs two theory courses with a group project run with the Scrum method, and in year two you take on cases for real companies. Year three includes exchange at a partner university and an internship at an internationally oriented organisation in the Netherlands or abroad, with minors and an honours programme as options, and year four ends with a graduation research project. Graduates become financial managers, business analysts, controllers, management accountants, treasury managers or entrepreneurs, or continue to a master such as Business Studies.

name: Jazz
overview: Your main instrument or voice is taught in one-to-one lessons with professional jazz musicians, alongside ensemble work in big band, vocal ensemble and small groups, music theory applied to playing, piano skills for non-pianists, and a repertoire of jazz standards with melody, accompaniment and improvisation. You perform in public from the start, take masterclasses with guest musicians, join themed project weeks and studio recording projects, and can spend a third-year exchange at conservatories in Europe or America. Groningen offers De Oosterpoort and a local club circuit. Graduates build portfolio careers combining performing, composing and arranging, and teaching, or continue to the Master of Music New York Jazz.

name: Marketing Management
overview: The first year covers international marketing, corporate communication, sales and business development, economics and organisation theory, and intercultural competence. You work in international groups on real company assignments and integrated projects, take part in a two-day hackathon, and finish with a graduation project commissioned by an external organisation. Year three includes an internship and a 30-credit minor at Hanze or a partner university abroad, and an honours programme is available. Graduates work in social media and digital marketing, account management, communications and sales management or start their own businesses, or continue to the MSc Business Studies.

name: Mechanical Engineering
overview: The first year covers product analysis, applied mechanics, energy technology, materials engineering, manufacturing technology and professional skills. You learn by doing: real engineering challenges for actual clients from the start, lab practicals, and hands-on work with small systems such as combustion engines, drives and installations. Year two includes a placement at a company of your choice, and year three allows a minor at Hanze, another Dutch university or abroad. The programme has a focus on the energy transition through the EnTranCe centre of expertise, and an honours track exists. Graduates work as power plant, installations or maintenance engineers, in R&D or technical sales, or continue to a master such as Renewable Energy.

name: Physiotherapy
overview: Year one covers anatomy, pathology, patient examination, evidence-based practice, conversation skills and professional development, and year two moves to heart and lung conditions, neurological disorders such as dementia and Parkinson disease, and complex movement problems. You practise on each other, work on projects for real clients and do short placements in year one, followed by external clinical placements and a graduation placement in years three and four. Minors, for example in Physiotherapy & Sport, or an exchange abroad are possible. Graduates work in hospitals, clinics, rehabilitation, private practice, gyms, schools and occupational health, or continue to a master.

name: Popular Culture
overview: Year one is organised around six group projects, such as exploring pop culture trends by theme, pitching concepts to clients, learning artistic direction and getting media attention for social issues, next to your own individual projects. Year two adds design research, concept development and grant applications, and you work in a production house, labs and in-depth core subjects within communities of learners. Year three brings an internship at cultural organisations or a minor in the Netherlands or abroad, and year four ends with an essay, an artistic concept and a realised performance production. Graduates work as performers, songwriters, producers, filmmakers, festival developers or podcasters, or continue to the MA Fine Art and Design.

name: Sport Studies
overview: The programme looks at sport through three values: its health, economic and social value. Throughout the degree you complete challenges, practical assignments in professional organisations, with work-based learning each year, plus a compulsory Outdoor Experience in year one and a Wintersport Experience in year two. You can use campus facilities such as the Equipment Centre, Sports Field Lab and Swimming School, choose electives, study abroad during a challenge, or join the honours education. Graduates work as sport marketers, event managers, sports entrepreneurs, coaches, policy officers or community developers, or continue to a master such as Healthy Ageing Professional.

name: African Studies
overview: You study Africa from an Africa-centred perspective, combining history, linguistics with Swahili language learning, anthropology, literature and cultural studies, area studies and sociology, with attention to ethnicity, gender and socio-economic background. In your second year you spend a semester in an African country for language immersion and courses at a local university. You learn to build and use databases and visual research tools, and to produce documentaries, podcasts and blogs. You can shape the degree around a discipline, a theme, the continent or a particular region, and draw on the African Studies Centre Leiden and its specialist library.

name: Archaeology
overview: The programme covers past societies, cultures and human behaviour, combining archaeological theory with practice and a broad view of the discipline. You take part in national and international fieldwork, work in laboratory practicals and join the research projects of staff. Contemporary issues such as migration, globalisation and climate change are seen through an archaeological lens, and you can focus on heritage in society, including policy and the heritage of migrant communities. Graduates find work in fields such as heritage management and museums, or continue to a master.

name: Cultural Anthropology and Development Sociology
overview: Four themes run through the programme: sustainability, diversity, digitalisation and methodology. Topics range from climate change and low-carbon futures to social media use, gender, racism, LGBTQIA+ rights, homelessness, food habits and child labour. You do fieldwork in the Netherlands and abroad, internships with organisations and communities, and use creative research methods such as photography, film, zine-making and drawing. Lectures and seminars give the theory, and the degree prepares you to support individuals, groups and communities affected by pressing social issues.

name: English Language and Culture
overview: You study the structure and acquisition of English, literature from Shakespeare to contemporary authors, the culture of Britain and other English-speaking countries, and Old and Middle English texts in the original, while building advanced spoken and written English. Language change is linked to societal change over time. Teaching is in English with a personal approach between students and lecturers, and specialisation courses in years two and three let you tailor the programme. Year three can include a minor, an internship or study abroad. Graduates move into academic careers, the public and private sectors, or media and cultural institutions such as film festivals, or continue to a master in literary studies.

name: Arts, Media and Society
overview: You study modern and contemporary visual art forms, from painting, photography and installation art to video art, bio-art, games, performance and digital media art, and how art relates to society and to the role of media in that relationship. The programme also links art to fields such as science and politics, and brings in sociology, cultural representation, cinema and contemporary media studies. You gain hands-on experience through research projects, field trips to museums, galleries and media institutions, and guest lectures by artists, scholars and scientists. Leiden gives easy access to museums and galleries in The Hague, Amsterdam and Rotterdam, and the degree prepares you for academia or the public or private sector.

name: Data Science and Artificial Intelligence
overview: You build a foundation in computer science and computational thinking, mathematics and statistics, programming, algorithms and information processing, and apply it to machine learning, cognitive science and artificial intelligence. Teaching is directly inspired by current research, and you can take part in research projects. The degree is run by LIACS, the Leiden Institute of Advanced Computer Science, and trains you as a computer scientist able to develop AI systems.

name: Dutch Studies
overview: You study the Dutch language, from beginner to advanced level, together with Dutch culture, history, society and ways of thinking. Classes are in Dutch from the first semester, so you learn through immersion and alongside Dutch students, in the historic city of Leiden, an international centre of Dutch studies. A one-year option combines language modules with electives such as Dutch Painting and Dutch Debates. Graduates can teach Dutch, work for international organisations connected to the Netherlands, or continue to a master focused on Dutch language or culture.

name: International Studies
overview: You approach global developments through history, politics, economics and culture, with lectures from several disciplines and language study tied to your region. You choose one of eight regional specialisations: Africa, East Asia, Europe, Latin America, the Middle East, North America, Russia and Eurasia, or South Asia and Southeast Asia, each with its own language options. In year three the PRINS course is a 12-week consultancy project in which teams tackle real challenges for organisations such as UN agencies, War Child Alliance and the Dutch Ministry of Foreign Affairs. The programme is based in The Hague, seat of the Dutch government, and prepares you for academia or the public or private sector.

name: Liberal Arts and Sciences: Global Challenges (Leiden University College)
overview: Global challenges such as climate change, conflict and inequality organise the programme, and you look at them through several disciplines before specialising, learning to see connections between fields. Classes are small and interactive, averaging about 18 students, with plenty of discussion and debate. You then major in one of five areas: Culture, History and Society; Earth, Energy and Sustainability; Governance, Economics and Development; International Justice; or World Politics. The college is in The Hague, with its ministries, international organisations and NGOs close by for professional contacts.

name: Linguistics
overview: You learn how language works: sound systems and syntax, how children acquire language, how languages compare, how endangered languages are documented and how languages change over time. Teaching happens in small classes with regular contact with teachers, and experimental work uses four language labs: Babylab, EEG, phonetics and eye-tracking. In year two you choose a specialisation: Descriptive Linguistics, Language and Cognition, Comparative Indo-European Linguistics, or the Dutch-taught Language in Use. The research behind the field feeds practical applications such as help for speech disorders, language software and preserving endangered languages.

name: Philosophy: Global and Comparative Perspectives
overview: You explore questions about reality, the mind and society through philosophical traditions from China, India, East Asia, Africa and the Arab world as well as Western philosophy from antiquity to the present, including ethics taught in tutorial seminars. Teaching centres on small tutorial groups for in-depth discussion, lectures by internationally known scholars, skills training and mentoring by senior students. You can tailor the curriculum to your interests, use the Asian Library collections, and add a semester abroad or an international internship. The training in critical thinking and handling complex information suits many employers, and a master such as Modern European Philosophy is an option.

name: Political Science: International Relations and Organisations
overview: You study global affairs and diplomacy, with courses such as Introduction to International Organisations, International Security and Introduction to International Relations, plus academic skills. Themes include conflict resolution, terrorism, peace and security, poverty, refugee crises, humanitarian cooperation, nuclear weapons reduction and globalisation, with a focus on major powers such as China, Russia, the USA and the EU and on bodies such as the UN, NATO, the IMF and the World Bank. You develop research, writing and presentation skills and write a thesis. The programme is based in The Hague, a UN city with many international organisations, embassies and NGOs.

name: Psychology (International Bachelor in Psychology)
overview: The programme gives a broad overview of the sub-areas of psychology, beginning with foundations such as bio-neuropsychology, which covers brain anatomy and how internal processes shape behaviour and psychological disorders. Lectures are interactive and often given by several specialists, and work groups use case examples from clinical practice and video analysis of real situations such as neuropsychological assessments. Halfway through you choose three specialisation courses in the areas that interest you. Studying in English also builds communication and cross-cultural collaboration skills.

name: Science for Sustainable Societies
overview: The programme rests on three pillars: planet, with environmental biology, industrial ecology, earth system science and ecological modelling; people, with anthropology, environmental psychology and human-environment relationships; and politics, with environmental governance, policy mechanisms and social transition. Large lectures are combined with small discussion seminars, and learning is project-based, with fieldwork, site visits to see environmental impacts, hands-on assignments and living labs. You gain skills in project management, programming, modelling and GIS, preparing you to contribute to the sustainability sector.

name: Security Studies
overview: You study security through political science, law, economics and history, using cases such as Syria, terrorism and counterterrorism, the Fukushima disaster, the SARS epidemic and the role of media, with attention to crisis management and governance. Teaching follows an Explore, Understand, Do approach, with lectures paired with skills labs in small groups, case studies that bring in current events, and academic and professional skills training. The programme is in The Hague, known as a city of peace, justice and security, and combines research with a practical orientation.

name: Urban Studies
overview: Four themes structure the degree: the sustainable city, the multicultural city, the safe city and the healthy city, set against theories of urban development, the history of cities and future urban trends. You learn in the classroom and in actual urban environments, on field trips to Dutch cities, through individual and group research projects, and in methods courses on observation, interviews, social network analysis and spatial analysis. In year two you specialise in one of the four themes, and year three offers an internship, exchange or minor, then a research lab with your thesis. Graduates move into academia, business or the public sector, or into a research or technical master.

name: South and Southeast Asian Studies
overview: You study the history, cultures and politics of South and Southeast Asia, including development and inequality, ethnic and religious conflict, political and cultural movements and the tension between modernity and tradition, and learn one language: Hindi, Sanskrit, Tibetan or Indonesian. You specialise in either modern societies or classical cultures, with lectures, seminars and language classes. In the third year you spend a semester in the region, at Gadjah Mada University in Yogyakarta, the University of Hyderabad or the Rangjung Yeshe Institute in Kathmandu depending on your language, and write a BA dissertation.

name: American Studies
overview: You study American society, politics, history, culture and language, including American literature, media and the arts, political institutions and the role of the United States in global affairs. Teaching is fully in English, with a strong focus on building written and spoken English at a professional level and on communication skills. Study abroad in the United States and internships are possible. The degree is a specialisation within the Bachelor of Arts in English Language and Culture at the Faculty of Arts in Nijmegen. Graduates work in international relations, education, journalism and other fields that value analytical and communication skills.

name: Artificial Intelligence
overview: The programme combines mathematics and computing science with psychology and neuroscience, logic and linguistics, with a special place for understanding and simulating the brain. Programming is taught from the basics at a pace suited to beginners, first-year students get mentoring support, and electives let you shape your own programme or spend part of it studying abroad. The programme works closely with several research institutes. Graduates work in education, research, healthcare, telecommunications, ICT, transport and financial services, and many are hired before they graduate.

name: Arts and Culture Studies
overview: You study cultural expressions across visual arts, literature, pop and classical music, film, television and theatre, using theoretical, historical, political and social perspectives. Questions include what counts as art, how popular culture relates to society, and how Western and non-Western views differ. Classes are small, interactive and international, and the degree leaves room for a minor and free electives. Graduates work as programme curators for theatres or festivals, reviewers of books or films, or government policy officers, in cultural organisations, government, publishing, research institutes or education.

name: Biology
overview: The programme covers seven domains of biology, from evolution, brain function and plant genetics to ecology, the effects of climate change on biodiversity, disease diagnosis and the chemistry of DNA and RNA. Teaching is interactive and team-based, with laboratory work in modern research facilities and internships at three research institutes (RIBES, RIMLS and DCN). After the foundation year you specialise and design your own profile, choosing courses from both biology and medical biology. Graduates work as researchers, teachers, consultants, policymakers or managers in profit and non-profit organisations.

name: Chemistry
overview: You study organic, physical and biochemistry alongside the mathematical and physical concepts behind molecular processes. Lectures are combined with thorough practical training: through experiments you study chemical reactions and use specialised techniques that rely on lasers and magnetic fields to study materials. With more than 25 chemistry research groups working on sustainability, drug development, data storage and the origin of life, you can choose the direction in which to specialise. Graduates work in industrial or university research, in education with a teaching qualification, or in consulting and management, or continue to related master programmes such as Molecular Life Sciences.

name: Computing Science
overview: You learn programming, how software works, how data is represented digitally, the mathematical and logical principles behind computing, how hardware is built into computers and networks, and how to protect IT systems through cybersecurity. Practical work includes GiPHouse, a student software company that works for real customers, and the New Devices Lab for experimenting with new gadgets, as well as courses on processor assembly language. Cyber security and AI are particular strengths of the Nijmegen programme. Graduates take IT roles across many sectors, and most find work before they graduate; the university AI master is a related option.

name: Economics and Business Economics
overview: The first year introduces the foundations of economics and three areas in which you can later specialise: accounting, finance, and international economics and policy. You develop an analytical perspective and learn research methods that connect theory to real-world questions. After year one you choose one of the three specialisation tracks. Most students continue to a master, and others work in consulting, banking, insurance or government organisations, in roles that call for rigorous economic analysis and prediction.

name: English Language and Culture
overview: You study the English language and linguistics, literature from English-speaking regions, including classics of high and popular culture, and the culture, history, social relations and customs of Great Britain and other English-speaking communities. Teaching is fully in English, with a strong focus on language development and communication skills, and the degree includes study abroad and hands-on internship experience. You follow either the English Language and Culture pathway or the American Studies pathway. Graduates work in communication, education, and culture and heritage.

name: International Business Administration
overview: You study international management together with psychology and sociology, communication and economics, law, marketing, human resources management and strategy, with a focus on responsible and sustainable organisations and entrepreneurship. The aim is to understand how organisations create social and economic value, and you build research skills for critically assessing scientific knowledge. A flexible semester in year three lets you follow your own interests, with optional study abroad and international internships.

name: International Business Communication
overview: You study language and communication theory applied to business, with intercultural communication, professional English and an optional Spanish specialisation, and learn to analyse language and communication processes scientifically. Classes are small and interactive, and scenario-based projects, such as designing an advertising campaign or developing a marketing plan, apply the theory directly while building consultancy, report-writing and research skills. Study abroad, a minor and free electives are possible. Graduates work in multinational companies, government organisations, NGOs, consultancy firms and educational institutions.

name: Molecular Life Sciences
overview: The first year builds on physics and mathematics, chemistry and biology, and looks at molecular processes from a biomedical angle: how cells work in health and disease and how multicellular organisms function. You learn through lectures, seminars and hands-on lab experiments in high-tech research facilities. Ten years after graduating, those without a PhD tend to hold managerial roles in technological settings, while PhD holders move into specialist positions with management responsibility or research roles at universities in the Netherlands and abroad.

name: Natural Sciences
overview: Physics, chemistry, biology and mathematics are taught at their intersection in a broad but rigorous first year, with extensive guidance from accessible teaching staff and laboratory work. Later you specialise in one of three directions: physical-chemical, biological-physical or biological-chemical, with advanced topics such as quantum mechanics, nanoscience, biophysics, DNA techniques and the analysis of molecular biological data. Graduates work in industry on scientific innovations such as solar cells, microchips and biodegradable plastics, in research needing interdisciplinary approaches, or as teachers, who are in high demand.

name: Philosophy, Politics and Society
overview: The first year introduces Western philosophy through four courses on its history, plus systematic courses in political philosophy, ethics, metaphysics and philosophical anthropology and the philosophy of science, alongside four courses in academic skills and methods. Classes are interactive, and in years two and three you follow modules of three courses on themes such as global justice, human rights, digital technology and ecological challenges, finishing with a bachelor thesis. Most students continue to a specialised master, and graduates work in policy analysis, think tanks, journalism, government, consultancy and NGOs.

name: Psychology
overview: You study human behaviour, mind and emotion: how the brain controls behaviour, how people develop from infancy to old age, and how environment and social context shape thinking, action and feeling. Research areas are Brain & Cognition, Development & Mental Health, and Behaviour & Environment, and practical research is part of the training. From year two you choose more of your own courses, and in year three you can study abroad, for example in Australia, Japan or South Africa. Graduates work in aid, education, human resources, public policy, counselling, training, coaching, sport and advertising.

name: American Studies
overview: First-year courses include The Americas, Theories of Culture, American Politics, a course on how identities are mediated in stories and one on Latin American and Canadian literature, taught in seminars with close contact with faculty. You write papers and also produce TED talks, editorials, exhibits and apps, and practise writing and speaking in American Studies in Practice. In year two you choose among a Media specialisation, Global USA and changing special topics, and you can spend a semester at a partner university in the United States, take a minor, and write a BA thesis. Graduates work in journalism, banking, culture, government and communications, or move on to master programmes such as Euroculture or Digital Humanities.

name: Applied Mathematics
overview: The first year covers analysis, calculus, linear algebra, linear systems, probability, graph theory, mechanics and relativity for mathematicians, and scientific programming, shared with the Mathematics degree so you can still switch. You learn to formulate and analyse abstract models of real systems, for example simulating the dynamics of a bicycle with numerical methods and code, and complete a research project in the final year. In years two and three you specialise in Numerical Mathematics or Systems, Control and Optimization, and an optional study period abroad is available. Graduates go on to the Applied Mathematics master, research and PhD positions, research institutes, consulting, finance and industry, or teaching.

name: Applied Physics
overview: The first year covers calculus, linear algebra, mechanics and relativity, electricity and magnetism, mathematical physics, computational methods, two physics laboratory courses and a course on the physics of modern technology. The programme stays deliberately broad, so you can postpone specialising until year two, and it is tied to research institutes for advanced materials, particle physics, energy and sustainability, and astronomy. An optional exchange semester abroad is possible, and the study association arranges company visits. Graduates work as consultants, researchers, technical innovators and analysts in industry, research institutes such as TNO, or banking and management consulting, or continue to a master in Applied Physics or Nanoscience.

name: Artificial Intelligence
overview: Year one includes introductions to AI, neuroscience and logic, imperative programming, algorithms and data structures, cognitive psychology, general linguistics, autonomous systems, calculus, linear algebra and statistics. You work on weekly assignments and real-world projects in international teams, and finish with a bachelor project under a researcher. You choose a specialisation from Computational Neuroscience, Hybrid Intelligence, Language and AI, Machine Learning and Robotics, and a period abroad is optional. Graduates work as machine learning engineers, data scientists, robotics engineers or software developers in software companies, research institutions, hospitals and banks, or continue to a master in Computational Cognitive Science or AI.

name: Arts, Culture and Media
overview: Year one covers audiovisual arts, the role of the arts in culture and the sociology of the arts, and you choose a main discipline of film, music or theatre, with literature or visual arts as a second art form. Later years deepen your art form and its philosophical and theoretical grounding, in seminars, group projects, a theatre project shown in local venues and visits to productions and festivals in Groningen. You choose between Arts Policy and Cultural Entrepreneurship or Analysis and Criticism, and the fifth semester can be a career minor, a pre-master or time abroad. Graduates work in theatre companies, concert halls, museums, publishing and media, or continue to master programmes such as Arts in Society or Film and Contemporary Audiovisual Media.

name: Astronomy
overview: Year one rests on calculus, linear algebra, mechanics and relativity, electricity and magnetism, mathematical physics and programming, with Introduction to Astronomy and Observational Astronomy, which uses the university's own observatory. Year two adds quantum physics, thermodynamics, waves and optics, and courses on the physics of stars, galaxies and radiative processes, taught through lectures and tutorials. In year three you carry out a research project in a research group and can choose a general astronomy minor or one on instrumentation and informatics. The programme links to the ASTRON and SRON institutes. Graduates go on to PhD research, technology roles with satellite and telescope companies, or business positions such as strategy and risk assessment.

name: Biology
overview: The first year covers cell and molecular biology, biostatistics, genetics, ecology and evolution, microbiology, physiology and behavioural neuroscience, taught in intensive three-week courses with practicals, fieldwork and independent study. You then choose a major in Ecology and Evolution, Molecular Life Sciences, Behaviour and Neurosciences, or Biomedical Sciences, the last partly at the University Medical Center Groningen. A third-year minor semester can be spent abroad, and you complete a research project and a bachelor thesis. Graduates work as researchers, environmental advisors, ecologists, policy advisors, science communicators or teachers, or continue to a master in fields such as marine biology or neurosciences.

name: Biomedical Engineering
overview: You combine mathematics, physics, biology and engineering, with first-year courses in anatomy and physiology, cell biology, microbiology, materials science, biomaterials, biomechanics and the design of biomedical products. Projects tackle problems such as designing artificial heart valves or MRI analysis software, backed by physics, microbiology and imaging labs. Some courses are taught by medical experts at the University Medical Center Groningen, and you can take a minor in Biomaterials Science and Engineering, Medical Device Design or Medical Imaging before a bachelor research project. Most graduates continue to the Biomedical Engineering master, leading to roles in medical device R&D, PhD research, hospitals, certification bodies and start-ups.

name: Chemistry
overview: Early courses cover concepts of chemistry, organic, inorganic and physical chemistry, biochemistry, spectroscopy and mathematics for chemistry, combining theory with hands-on work in modern laboratories, including synthesis, analysis and biochemistry labs. You can join staff research projects early on and then specialise in Smart Materials, Chemistry of Life, or Sustainable Chemistry and Energy. The programme is tied to the Stratingh Institute for Chemistry and the Zernike Institute for Advanced Materials, and a semester abroad is possible. Graduates work as industrial or scientific researchers, managers, in commercial roles or as teachers, or continue to a master such as Chemistry, Biomolecular Sciences or Nanoscience.

name: Communication and Information Studies
overview: Year one looks at how communication works in text, talk and other forms, with courses on persuasion and argumentation, intercultural communication, qualitative research methods and academic English. In year two you apply it in team projects on real cases, with corporate and organisational communication, digital and social media, health communication and quantitative methods. The fifth semester can be a minor, a career minor with an internship, or study abroad, and the degree ends with an independent research thesis. Dutch speakers can follow a Dutch track. Graduates work as communications officers, consultants, editors, press officers, journalists or marketing managers, or continue to a master such as Communication Studies or Digital Humanities.

name: Computing Science
overview: The first year covers programming fundamentals, object-oriented programming, algorithms and data structures in C, computer architecture, networks, logic, discrete structures, calculus, linear algebra and information systems. There is creative freedom in projects and practicals, with quick feedback on programming work, and opportunities for an internship in a research group or company or for study abroad. The programme is linked to research groups in computer architecture, distributed systems, intelligent systems, software engineering and scientific visualisation. Graduates work as software developers, data engineers, cybersecurity experts, machine learning specialists or game developers, or continue to a master in Computing Science or AI.

name: Data Science and Society
overview: You study programming in Python, databases and SQL, big data analytics, statistical and machine learning, visualising data and statistical inference alongside science and technology studies, the governance of innovation and human rights in the digital age. Learning is discussion-based, with one-to-one mentoring and field projects for partner organisations such as the Dutch statistics bureau CBS, Datamaran and TEXroad, in Leeuwarden with its DataFryslan initiative. In year two you specialise in AI and Society or in Cognitive Technology, and year three offers study abroad or a minor, plus a bachelor thesis. Graduates become data engineers, data scientists, data analysts, data protection officers or policy advisors.

name: Chemical Engineering
overview: Year one is shared with Chemistry, covering mathematics for chemistry, organic, physical and inorganic chemistry, spectroscopy and an introduction to chemical engineering. Year two turns to thermodynamics, transport phenomena, reactors, separation processes, polymer chemistry and green chemistry. Laboratory practicals run throughout, with a process design project and a bachelor research project carried out with industry partners, and a semester abroad is optional. The programme draws on companies such as Shell, BASF and AkzoNobel. Graduates become chemical or energy engineers, product developers or researchers, or continue to a master in Chemical Engineering or Energy & Environmental Sciences.

name: Art History
overview: Year one is a survey from Classical Antiquity to the present, with visual analysis, iconography, materials and techniques, garden heritage, and art and architecture since 1750; year two adds contemporary art, architectural theory, the Italian Renaissance and landscape design. Fridays are usually reserved for excursions, within the Netherlands and to cities such as Berlin, London, Florence and Vienna, and a practice lab and a thesis complete the training. You can specialise in Modern & Contemporary Art, Early Modern Art, Architecture & Urbanism, or Landscape History. Graduates work in museums, heritage management, journalism, publishing and teaching, or continue to a master such as Curatorial Studies.

name: Econometrics and Operations Research
overview: The first year builds mathematics (calculus, linear algebra, analysis), probability, programming, finance, microeconomics, operations research modelling and statistical modelling, and year two adds convexity and optimisation, macroeconomics, game theory, econometrics, stochastic and discrete operations research and actuarial courses on life and risk insurance. In all three years you run a company in the EOR Game simulation, working in small groups with personal contact with lecturers. You choose a profile in Econometrics, Operations Research, Actuarial Science or Mathematical Economics, and year three offers a minor or study abroad. Most graduates continue to a master, then work as quantitative analysts, consultants, actuaries or risk managers.

name: Economics and Business Economics
overview: The first year covers microeconomics, macroeconomics, financial accounting, statistics, data analysis, international economics, finance and investments, the Dutch economy and writing and presenting, and ends with a research project. From year two you choose a profile: Business Economics, Economics, or International Economics and Sustainable Development. Teamwork and real-world data projects are central, with mentor groups, and year three offers a minor, a semester abroad or an internship, plus an empirical bachelor thesis. Graduates work as financial analysts, policy advisors, risk analysts, consultants or researchers, or continue to a master in finance, economics or a related field.

name: English Language and Culture
overview: Year one includes medieval English literature, an overview of English literatures from Chaucer and Shakespeare to Austen and Atwood, English linguistics and the structure of language in social contexts, and Professional English for academic writing, presentations and debate. Year two adds cognitive aspects of language and identities and ideologies from medieval to modern times, with options such as sociolinguistics, Arthurian studies and early modern literature. Classes are small, a placement and a minor are possible, and you can study at partner universities in the UK and Ireland. About 80 percent continue to a master, and graduates work in publishing, politics, cultural organisations, tourism, communications and education.

name: European Languages, Cultures and Politics
overview: The first year introduces European language and society, European culture and literature, and European politics and society, together with progressive language training in your major language: German, English, French, Italian, Dutch, Russian, Spanish or Swedish. Language units are intensive and usually in small groups, and from year two you follow one of three profiles: European Language and Society, European Culture and Literature, or European Politics and Society. Year three includes a minor, which can be a work placement, research or teacher training, or study abroad, and a bachelor thesis. Graduates work as policy officers, communications consultants, journalists, teachers or translators, or continue to a master such as Euroculture.

name: Global Politics and Sustainability
overview: Year one combines environmental systems and climate science, political and economic analysis, research methods, and the sustainable energy transition and leadership for sustainability. In year two you follow a Planet track on energy futures and resource use or a Politics track on power, inequality and political and economic systems. Teachers act as coaches, and living-lab projects with outside partners, such as Amnesty International and Friesland social organisations, tackle real sustainability challenges. Year three has an exchange, internship or minor and a bachelor thesis. Graduates work as policy advisors, researchers or consultants in government, NGOs and business, or continue to a master such as Political Science or Environmental Sciences.

name: History
overview: Year one covers ancient, medieval, early modern and contemporary history, Dutch history in a global setting, historical sources and academic writing, and year two adds modern history, cultural, political and economic and social approaches, historical theory and a region of your choice for deeper study. Lecture courses are combined with working groups, independent research with papers and presentations, and a bachelor thesis. The fifth semester can be a career minor with a placement, study abroad or another minor. Graduates work as policy officers, journalists, museum professionals or educators, or continue to a master such as History and Heritage Consultancy or Euroculture.

name: Human Geography and Planning
overview: You study urbanism and planning, economic, population and rural geography, migration and development, culture and place, governance and physical geography, with statistics, GIS and qualitative and quantitative research methods. Fieldwork takes place every year, and first-year students are paired with senior mentors in small groups. Year three offers an optional internship with, for example, a local government planning department, a semester abroad, and a bachelor project. Graduates work as spatial planning advisors in consultancies, project managers in local government, researchers at housing associations or geography teachers, or continue to one of the specialised master programmes in spatial sciences.

name: Industrial Engineering and Management
overview: About two thirds of the programme is technical and one third business: first-year courses include calculus, linear algebra, programming, modelling and simulation, transport phenomena and statistics, together with organisational behaviour, management accounting, industrial marketing and global supply chains. A capstone project on the design of complex systems and a final-year integration project solving concrete problems with companies give practical experience. You specialise in Production Technology and Logistics, Sustainable Process Engineering, or Mechanical Engineering, and can study abroad in the third-year minor. Graduates work as process technologists, product managers or consultants in automotive, chemical, pharmaceutical and energy sectors.

name: Information Science
overview: First-year courses cover language technology, information science, programming from scratch, statistics, data manipulation, machine learning, humane AI in digital societies and web development. Teaching favours group projects over big exams, with real-world data challenges, software development exercises and collaborative co-creative AI work, balanced between theory and practice. Electives lean towards law and IT, business, AI, linguistics and communication, and the fifth semester can be a minor or study abroad before a bachelor thesis project. Graduates work as data scientists, software developers, analytics consultants or content managers, or continue to a master in Information Science or Natural Language Processing.

name: International and European Law
overview: Year one covers legal English and research skills, Dutch law as an example of legal skills, criminal law, legal history, contract and tort law, and an introduction to international and European law; year two adds comparative constitutional law, technology law, EU law, property law, law, power and politics and public international law. From year two you choose International and European Law or Technology Law. Everyone spends a semester abroad at a partner university in year three and writes a bachelor thesis. Almost all graduates continue to a master, and they work as diplomats, policy advisors, NGO and UN specialists or compliance officers.

name: International Business
overview: Year one covers global supply chain management, international business, financial accounting, organisational behaviour, economics, international marketing, statistics and international trade, and year two adds digital transformation, finance, ethics, cross-cultural management, global political economy and international business law. You work on real company cases, team projects and discussion seminars with guest speakers. In year three you choose a semester abroad, an internship or a minor such as data analytics, finance or innovation and entrepreneurship. Graduates work as export managers, international marketers, sales or product managers, or analysts, or continue to a master in International Business and Management, Finance or Marketing.

name: International Relations and International Organization
overview: First-year modules include Economics for Public Policy, the historical foundations of modern IR, Introduction to International Relations, contemporary global history, political systems of the world and theories for analysing IR; year two covers security studies, EU governance, global political economy, international law and research methods. Assignments are varied, from essays and research papers to video production and group presentations, with a language course along the way. You choose from about ten specialisation themes, take a minor in year three and write a bachelor thesis. Graduates work as policy advisors, lobbyists, journalists and researchers in governments, NGOs and international organisations, or continue to a master such as International Security.

name: Liberal Arts and Sciences
overview: The first years combine academic and professional skills, an introduction to academic research and core electives on the challenges of modern society, with research and methodology courses in the sciences, social sciences or humanities. Seminars are small and interactive, and you work in teams on real-world projects, often with outside partners, with a capstone project each year and a bachelor thesis. You major in Sciences, Social Sciences or Humanities, and choose a minor, an exchange abroad or an internship; a double degree track with Ca' Foscari University in Venice is available. About 84 percent of graduates continue to a master, in fields such as psychology, medicine or international relations.

name: Life Science and Technology
overview: Year one includes biochemistry, biophysics, calculus, mammalian cell biology, optics, organic chemistry, pharmaceutical analysis, physiology, programming for life sciences and thermodynamics, and year two adds inorganic chemistry, spectroscopy and microbiology. Practical lab courses run from the first year, and you finish with a research project in your area of specialisation, chosen in year three from pharmaceutical sciences, biology, chemistry or physics. The programme links to four research institutes, including those for biomolecular sciences, chemistry, advanced materials and pharmacy. Graduates typically continue to a master such as Biomolecular Sciences or Medical Pharmaceutical Sciences, leading to research, biomedical engineering, product development or teaching.

name: Mathematics
overview: The shared first year covers analysis, linear algebra, sets and numbers, probability, graph theory, linear systems, mechanics and relativity for mathematicians, and scientific programming, so you can still switch to Applied Mathematics. Later years add statistics, group theory, partial differential equations, complex analysis, functional analysis and numerical mathematics, with flexible electives in algebra, topology, probability and dynamical systems. You complete a first-year project, a research project and a bachelor thesis, and a double degree with Physics is possible. The degree leads to the Mathematics master and to work as a researcher, consultant, analyst or teacher, with employers such as Shell, Philips and ABN Amro.

name: Media Studies
overview: Year one introduces media studies, media and everyday life, how media past, present and future connect, and theories of audiences and uses, alongside professional writing and academic skills; year two covers representations in media, analysing media texts, production and use, and a research seminar. You choose a profile in Visual Culture, Cultural Industries, Digital Cultures, Journalism Studies, or Politics and Global Citizenship. A minor can be a career minor with an internship, or you can study abroad, and the degree ends with a bachelor thesis. Graduates work as strategy consultants, social media analysts, policy advisors, content producers and PR professionals, or continue to a master such as Journalism.

name: Physics
overview: The first year covers calculus, linear algebra, mechanics and relativity, electricity and magnetism, mathematical physics, computational methods and two physics laboratory courses, with introductory electives such as astronomy, medical physics, nanophysics and quantum topics. You gain hands-on lab experience, learn to turn complex theory into practical solutions, and complete a bachelor research project, with study abroad as an option. Specialisations include Nanophysics, Particle Physics, Energy & Environmental Physics, Biophysics & Medical Physics and physics education, linked to research institutes for advanced materials, particle physics and energy. Graduates continue to a master such as Physics or Nanoscience and work in research, industry, consultancy, analytics or teaching.

name: Psychology
overview: The first years cover biological, developmental, cognitive, social and cross-cultural psychology, personality and individual differences, the history of psychology, research methods and statistics, and professional methods such as test administration. You learn in small mentor-led groups, with research practicals in which you design and present studies, role-play exercises and a bachelor thesis on your own research project in year three. Professional areas include work and organisational psychology, clinical psychology and clinical neuropsychology, and you can study abroad through a minor or join the honours college. Graduates continue to a psychology master or one in neurosciences, and work as psychologists, market researchers or organisational consultants.

name: Religious Studies
overview: You begin with the major world religions, Christianity, Judaism, Islam, Buddhism and Hinduism, the concepts and methods of the study of religion, the anthropology, psychology, sociology and philosophy of religion, and religion in South Asia. Assessment leans on written assignments and research papers, year two includes Rituals in Theory and Practice, and year three has a thesis seminar and an independent bachelor thesis; Quranic Arabic is optional. A minor can be Spiritual Care, teacher training or study at another faculty, and an internship or exchange is possible. Graduates work in care, policy and management, education, church, culture and media, or continue to a master such as Religion, Conflict and Globalization.

name: Spatial Planning and Design
overview: Year one introduces the power of design, urbanism and planning, economic geography, research skills, statistics and GIS, with a Spatial Design Atelier for studio work; year two covers infrastructure and mobility, water management, governance dynamics, physical geography and research methods. Learning happens in studios, on excursions to see spatial projects in real life, in virtual environments and in team projects that reflect professional practice, ending with a bachelor thesis. Year three leaves room for a minor or exchange, and an honours college is available. Graduates work in policy for spatial planning, environment and mobility, in consulting and real estate development, or continue to one of 13 master programmes in spatial sciences.
